summary: Resolves three audit findings in TaskTracker's label integration: replace direct SQL cross-schema read with HTTP batch call, and transform two GET proxy endpoints to return Dataset.

classification.why_application: Changes are scoped to TaskTracker's label proxy endpoints and internal label-fetch helper. The fix applies app-specific route transformation and domain-shaped Dataset construction. No reusable platform capability is being added.
non_goals: Mutation proxy endpoints (POST attach, DELETE detach, PUT set): no change
Embedded labels field in list_tasks Dataset rows or TASK_SCHEMA (F-004): separate sprint
classification.not_platform: These changes are specific to TaskTracker's label proxy behavior and its Dataset shaping for task-related label reads.

consumes: LabelEngine POST /api/objects/labels/batch — BatchLabelsRequest { object_ids: list[str], object_type: str } → BatchLabelsResponse { labels: dict[str, list[{id, name, attached_at}]] }
LabelEngine GET /api/labels — label search by prefix → { labels: [{id, name}] }
platform_contracts.Dataset, DatasetMeta, ColumnSchema — canonical UI contract (R-CON-BP-04)
provides: GET /tasks/labels/search — Dataset with columns [id: string, name: string]
GET /tasks/{task_id}/labels — Dataset with columns [id: string, name: string, attached_at: date]
list_tasks continues to embed labels per-row via HTTP batch call (no SQL cross-schema access)
invariants: GET /tasks/labels/search and GET /tasks/{task_id}/labels return Dataset | ApiError — never a bespoke shape
fetch_labels_for_tasks does not hold a DB connection parameter; it uses _label_client() exclusively
The batch call uses object_type='task' consistently
failure_modes: LabelEngine unreachable: fetch_labels_for_tasks returns {} (empty map); list_tasks rows get empty labels list
LabelEngine unreachable on search_labels: upstream HTTP status propagated with Dataset fallback not required — ApiError acceptable
LabelEngine unreachable on get_task_labels: upstream HTTP status propagated — ApiError acceptable
LabelEngine returns non-200 on batch: fetch_labels_for_tasks returns {} silently

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /tasks/labels/search
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Search labels by prefix for autocomplete; returns Dataset with id and name columns

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return labels attached to a specific task; returns Dataset with id, name, attached_at columns

internal_flow.name: replace_fetch_labels_for_tasks
internal_flow.description: Remove the SQL implementation of fetch_labels_for_tasks (tasks.py:72–95). Replace with an HTTP call to POST /api/objects/labels/batch via _label_client(). Drop the conn parameter. Return type remains dict[str, list[dict]]. On non-200 response return {}. The call site in list_tasks (line ~231) drops the conn argument.
outputs: dict[str, list[{id, name, attached_at}]] keyed by task_id; empty dict on error or empty input

internal_flow.name: transform_search_labels
internal_flow.description: search_labels endpoint: after receiving the LabelEngine response, extract items from resp.json().get('labels', []). Construct Dataset with meta(object_type='label', label='Labels', total=len(items), page=1, page_size=len(items), row_actions=[]) and schema [id: string, name: string]. rows are [{id: item['id'], name: item['name']} for item in items]. Return via dataset_response(). On non-200 from LabelEngine, propagate error status using JSONResponse.
outputs: Dataset with id and name columns | JSONResponse with upstream error status

internal_flow.name: transform_get_task_labels
internal_flow.description: get_task_labels endpoint: after receiving the LabelEngine response, extract items from resp.json().get('labels', []). Construct Dataset with meta(object_type='task_label', label='Task Labels', total=len(items), page=1, page_size=len(items), row_actions=['delete']) and schema [id: string, name: string, attached_at: date]. rows are [{id: lbl['label_id'], name: lbl['label_name'], attached_at: lbl['attached_at']} for lbl in items]. Return via dataset_response(). On non-200 from LabelEngine, propagate error status using JSONResponse.
outputs: Dataset with id, name, attached_at columns | JSONResponse with upstream error status

internal_flow.name: update_shellentry_call_sites
internal_flow.description: Update four call sites in ShellEntry.tsx that consume bespoke label shapes. (a) Lines ~435–436: search_labels autocomplete in LabelPanel — change res.labels cast to res.rows.map(r => ({id: r.id as string, name: r.name as string})). (b) Lines ~732–733: search_labels autocomplete in TaskEditPanel — same transformation. (c) Lines ~893–895: get_task_labels initial load in TaskEditPanel — change res.labels cast to res.rows.map(r => ({label_id: r.id as string, label_name: r.name as string, attached_at: r.attached_at as string})). (d) Lines ~1102–1103: search_labels autocomplete in TaskCreatePanel.handleLabelQueryChange — same transformation as (a) and (b): res.rows.map(r => ({id: r.id as string, name: r.name as string})). The apiFetch generic type parameter changes from { labels: T } to a structural type with rows field for all four sites.
inputs: ShellEntry.tsx current call sites consuming { labels: [...] } shapes
outputs: ShellEntry.tsx four call sites consuming res.rows with correct field mapping

risks.risk: LabelEngine Sprint02 batch endpoint not yet deployed
risks.impact: fetch_labels_for_tasks will return {} on every call; list_tasks will show empty labels for all tasks until the service is available

risks.risk: LabelEngine batch response field name mismatch
risks.impact: Sprint02 architecture defines BatchLabelRecord as {id, name, attached_at}. The draft.md cites the same shape. If the actual deployed endpoint uses different field names, the row-building code in fetch_labels_for_tasks will silently produce empty or malformed label records.

The existing call sites use apiFetch<{ labels: T }>. Changing to consume res.rows requires the type parameter to be compatible with Dataset or to use a structural type asserting rows exists. If apiFetch enforces the generic strictly, a type assertion or import of Dataset type may be needed.

open_questions.question: Should search_labels propagate LabelEngine non-200 status codes directly, or wrap them in an api_error response? The draft does not specify error handling for the proxy endpoints.
